papers.title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?

summary.tldr: See2Think introduces a unified evaluation framework, See2ThinkBench and Visual Action-of-Thought (VAoT), to assess how multimodal models utilize intermediate visual states in reasoning across 1,200 visually dependent problems.
key_points: See2ThinkBench comprises 1,200 open-ended, visually dependent problems across 12 task categories, covering 2D structured, 3D scene, and real-world reasoning.
VAoT records textual thoughts, visual actions, rendered states, and subsequent reasoning under four controlled inference settings.
Evaluation of representative multimodal models shows visual reasoning is strongly model- and environment-dependent, with no single setting consistently dominating.
Process analysis indicates models select relevant visual operations, but faithful rendering is a bottleneck; high feedback uptake does not guarantee accuracy gains.
Models exhibit behavioral dependence on visual states, with accuracy dropping over 10 percentage points under task-relevant corrupted visual feedback.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how multimodal models use intermediate visual states is crucial for developing more reliable and interpretable visual reasoning systems.

papers.title: β-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: β-OPSD generalizes on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by introducing β as a controllable regularization parameter, enabling efficient approximation of policy optimization through logit mixing and outperforming vanilla OPSD in reasoning tasks.
key_points: Vanilla OPSD is identified as the β=1 member of a policy-optimization family, where β weights the KL penalty to a reference policy.
β-OPSD's optimal policy is derived as a geometric interpolation between a reference policy and a privileged teacher.
The closed-form solution of β-OPSD is approximated by mixing token-level logits from the reference and teacher policies, avoiding direct, high-variance reinforcement learning optimization.
Return-to-go credit assignment is incorporated to align token updates with sequence-level objectives.
Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate β-OPSD consistently outperforms vanilla OPSD in stability and performance.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more stable and performant approach to self-distillation for reasoning language models, reducing engineering effort and improving practical applicability.

papers.title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers

summary.tldr: Chimera introduces a hybrid visual diffusion backbone with Kimi Delta Attention, Multi-head Latent Attention, and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts, scaled using HeteroP for compute-optimal performance in high-resolution image and long video generation.
key_points: Chimera processes text, image, and video tokens in a single raster-ordered stream without positional embeddings, utilizing Kimi Delta Attention (O(N) complexity), interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention, and modality-aware short convolutions.
The architecture incorporates Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers to expand capacity while controlling activated compute.
HeteroP, a module-wise scaling scheme, transfers hyperparameters across width and depth based on functional fan-in and model depth, enabling Chinchilla-style compute-optimal scaling laws.
An 11B-parameter Chimera with 2B activated parameters demonstrated 7.3x compute efficiency compared to a full-attention Wan-2.1 2B baseline in pretraining diffusion loss.
Chimera extrapolates zero-shot from 5-second training clips to 30-second videos with only 6.5% FID degradation in the last five seconds, without length-specific fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a foundation for designing and scaling efficient long-context diffusion architectures, enabling high-resolution image and long video generation with reduced computational cost.

papers.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow

summary.tldr: ShadowDancer enables frame-level control of video world models by learning unified dynamics representations from video pairs that replay the same dynamics with independently resampled appearances, improving action transfer and long rollout.
key_points: ShadowDancer uses "shadow pairs," video pairs constructed at scale by a "Shadow Library," which replay identical dynamics with independently resampled appearances.
It employs "cross-shadow prediction" to learn actions by predicting one shadow from the other, discarding appearance variations and preserving dynamics.
This approach yields a unified dynamics representation that drives a block-causal world model, allowing any demonstrated clip to be a reusable action asset.
Experiments show improved action transfer and long action rollout compared to latent-action and interactive world model baselines, with an 86% blinded win rate in rollout comparisons.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows for precise, frame-level control of video world models using demonstrated actions without requiring action labels, motion estimators, or fine-tuning in new environments.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Execute Parent Orders?

summary.tldr: This paper introduces PACE, a hierarchical LLM framework for parent-order execution in algorithmic trading, outperforming existing methods without explicit market assumptions or task-specific training.
key_points: PACE (Plan-Ahead Controlled Execution) is a hierarchical framework decomposing parent-order execution into long-horizon planning and short-horizon execution.
PACE requires neither explicit market assumptions nor task-specific training, addressing limitations of prior approaches.
Experiments on Shenzhen Stock Exchange Level-1 data show PACE outperforms TWAP, Almgren-Chriss, and learning-based baselines, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.65 bps.
LLMs in PACE exhibit different trading behaviors than human investors, with higher model confidence correlating with better performance and earlier trading decisions.
summary.why_it_matters: This research demonstrates LLMs' capability to extend into "how to execute" in finance, potentially complementing human traders in execution decisions.

papers.title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed

summary.tldr: MemHarness is a framework for LLM agents that reconstructs retrieved past experiences based on the current context, rather than replaying them verbatim, to improve decision-making and prevent negative transfer.
key_points: MemHarness employs a unified policy model to critique and reconstruct retrieved experiences conditioned on the current state, generating context-grounded guidance.
The reconstructive ability is developed through end-to-end training using GRPO.
Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop demonstrate MemHarness outperforms pure RL and static memory-augmented baselines.
MemHarness shows strong robustness in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios.
The reconstruction objective prevents negative transfer and acts as latent guidance, improving intrinsic reasoning capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enhances LLM agent performance and adaptability by enabling dynamic memory utilization, leading to more robust and intelligent agents.

papers.title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models

summary.tldr: INTACT is an end-to-end JEPA that converts action-labeled, reward-free trajectories into a search-free intent-to-action interface using isomorphic architecture and action-law semantics.
key_points: INTACT uses an isomorphic architecture with shared parameters and a four-slot grammar for local and goal motion-intent backbone-input graphs.
It employs action-law semantics induced by a shared predictor for both local and goal motion-intent families, rather than pointwise latent equality.
Asymmetric endpoint gradients ground physical successors and fix future goals, integrating representation learning and control without pointwise latent matching.
The model achieves 85.78%, 100.00%, 97.67%, and 97.89% success on four LeWM tasks with one-epoch, zero-search models.
Direct inference takes 2.9-5.5 ms, and optional local CEM reduces sampling by 23.44 times while improving pure CEM by 16.00 points.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables efficient, search-free policy generation for world models, significantly reducing computational cost and improving performance in robotic control tasks.

papers.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger

summary.tldr: LedgerMind introduces a provenance-constrained state machine for multimodal agents, using a Structured Evidence Ledger to improve reasoning faithfulness and address common failure patterns beyond final-answer accuracy.
key_points: Multimodal agent trajectories are modeled as a provenance-constrained state machine, where tool outputs are normalized into a Structured Evidence Ledger.
Reasoning and decision claims must cite active ledger entries, with grounding checked at entity and numeric levels, and repair as typed state transitions without content amplification.

LedgerMind incorporates a Three-Layer Grounding Protocol, an Adaptive Dual-Path Dispatcher for question complexity, and an Event-Triggered Verification-and-Repair engine with provenance non-amplification guarantee.
The system targets failure patterns like unsupported intermediate reasoning, citation-backed entity hallucination (Phantom Grounding), over-reasoning, and repair-time amplification.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a more robust and verifiable method for multimodal agent reasoning, leading to more trustworthy AI systems.

papers.title: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale

summary.tldr: Echoverse introduces deep, evolving synthetic environments for training computer-use agents, compiling specifications into stateful applications with database-graded tasks and a co-evolution loop for environment and model improvement.
key_points: Echoverse compiles specifications into stateful applications with tasks graded against the application's own database.
A co-evolution loop uses graded rollouts to repair environments, tasks, and verifiers, and as training signals for the model.
Training a 9B model on twelve Echoverse environments improved performance from 36.5% to 67.1% across fourteen evaluation splits.
Deep environments increased live-site accuracy (80.0% to 85.0% and 48.0% to 65.0%), while shallow ones decreased it (80.0% to 75.0%).
Repairing a single environment lifted the model trained on it from 16.2% to 38.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables scalable and effective training of computer-use agents by providing dynamic, high-quality synthetic environments that adapt to model performance.

papers.title: Σ-Mem: An Online Reliability Memory for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: Σ-Mem is an online reliability memory for LLM-based multi-agent systems that records and updates historical competence and peer relationship evidence to enable adaptive coordination.
key_points: Σ-Mem maintains historical competence evidence for individual peers and peer relationship evidence across the peer set as real symmetric states.
Evidence is updated from post-decision correctness feedback, with spectral change bounded by Weyl's inequality for stable online adaptation.
The memory offers a general write-and-read interface for residual steering, response-free peer routing, or reliability-weighted voting.
Evaluated across five Qwen-family models, Σ-Mem adapts to counterfactual reliability shifts and generalizes to unseen peers and task domains.
summary.why_it_matters: This system provides a reusable foundation for adaptive coordination in multi-agent LLM systems by enabling models to learn and leverage peer reliability.

papers.title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation

summary.tldr: Explorative Modeling (XMs) introduces a new pretraining axis by factoring the training loop to explore K candidate matches, improving generative model performance and enabling end-to-end reconstructive generative modeling.
key_points: Explorative Modeling (XMs) factors the training loop, exploring K candidate matches between model generations and data, training on the best match to commit to modes.
Increasing exploration improves performance across continuous and discrete domains (images, video, language), with gains increasing from 7% to 36% as data scales and 13% to 23% as models grow.
XMs improve FLOP efficiency by 4.1x, sample efficiency by 6.2x, and parameter efficiency by 47%, achieving 1.43 FID on ImageNet without guidance.
XMs enable end-to-end reconstructive generative modeling, matching diffusion on control tasks with 16-256x fewer inference steps.
summary.why_it_matters: This new paradigm offers significant efficiency gains and performance improvements for generative models, potentially leading to more scalable and effective AI generation.

papers.title: Multi-Head Attention Residuals

summary.tldr: Multi-Head Attention Residuals (MHAR) improve Transformer performance by allowing per-subspace attention over depth history, addressing limitations of single-query attention residuals.
key_points: MHAR reshapes the routing query into H per-subspace heads, each with its own softmax over depth history, enabling block-diagonal reads.
MHAR improves validation loss on a Nemotron-based corpus by -0.061 (100M), -0.149 (350M), and -0.140 (1B) over standard Transformers.
Optimal head count (H) is 4 or 8 across scales; H=8 is adopted for large models, with over-splitting (H=16) reducing gains.
Fused Triton routing kernels increase attention-residual training throughput to 0.55-0.88x of baseline, maintaining near-baseline peak memory.
Identity-preserving conversion with delta attention residuals yields +3.2 on GSM8K and +3.1 on GPQA for an 8B model mid-training.
summary.why_it_matters: MHAR offers a computationally efficient method to enhance Transformer performance and scalability by improving information propagation across model depth.

papers.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability

summary.tldr: This paper systematically explores filesystem-based memory for LLM agents, formalizing its structure and evaluating organization, evolution, and sustainability across various benchmarks.
key_points: Filesystem-based memory is formalized with three roles: a management agent for organization, a search agent for queries, and an execution agent for skill distillation.
The study varies memory shape (hierarchy, verbatim dump, chunk retrieval), stream scale, tool harness (sandboxed shell, memory-tool functions), and agent strengths.
Organized stores roughly halve retrieval cost for large material, demonstrating search economy.
Organization erodes for all but the strongest management agents during growth, and organization itself does not consistently improve answer quality.
Tool set changes can reshape the memory store as strongly as swapping the underlying model.
summary.why_it_matters: This research transforms filesystem-based memory from an untested assumption into a defined design space for LLM agent memory systems.

papers.title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes

summary.tldr: This work analyzes lossy verification in speculative decoding, classifying methods into truncation-based and collaborative verification, and identifies mechanisms for quality degradation and principles for stable generation.
key_points: Lossy verification schemes in speculative decoding can degrade generation quality by silently rewriting the decoding distribution.
Lossy verification methods are categorized into truncation-based verification and collaborative verification.
Truncation-based methods can suffer significant performance degradation due to distributional distortion compared to true truncation sampling.
Collaborative verification requires controlling the overshoot of draft probabilities relative to target probabilities to prevent low-quality outputs.
A diagnostic evaluation framework was constructed to analyze these methods across curated benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the mechanisms and trade-offs of lossy verification is crucial for developing efficient and stable speculative decoding methods for large language models.

papers.title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents

summary.tldr: Harness-G is a graph-structured retrieval framework that reformulates free-form query generation as finite action selection, addressing retrieval aliasing in RL search agents and improving QA performance.
key_points: Harness-G redesigns the policy-environment interface for retrieval, changing free-form query generation to finite action selection (selecting an evidence sentence/entity or answering).
The environment in Harness-G constructs the action menu, tracks retrieval state, and validates/executes choices, reducing linguistic aliasing and making same-state alternatives comparable.
Harness-G introduces Structured Non-myopic Credit (SNC), which uses a frozen answer scorer to compare selected actions with alternatives and assign downstream gains to enabling earlier actions.
Harness-G achieved the highest average F1 across six QA benchmarks, outperforming Graph-R1 by 10.74 points at 1.5B model scale and 3.98 points at 3B model scale.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly improves the performance of reinforcement learning search agents in question answering by addressing fundamental issues in retrieval formulation.

papers.title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models

summary.tldr: OmniScope is a training-free token compression framework for omnimodal LLMs that decouples audio and video relevance estimation using the query as a shared anchor, achieving significant speedup and memory reduction with minimal accuracy loss.
key_points: OmniScope addresses cross-modal salience mismatch by estimating audio and video relevance separately, guided by the query as a shared semantic anchor.
The framework allocates modality-specific token budgets and prunes visual tokens using an anchor-delta strategy to preserve global context and temporal changes.
Audio tokens are merged within each second to reduce redundancy while maintaining temporal continuity.

OmniScope achieves up to 3.53x prefill speedup and over 15% GPU memory reduction at 25% token retention, with only a 0.35-point average accuracy drop across four audio-video benchmarks and two Qwen2.5-Omni model scales.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more efficient inference for omnimodal large language models by significantly reducing computational overhead while maintaining high accuracy.

papers.title: Is Deep Research Reliable? Misleading Knowledge Induces False Conclusions

summary.tldr: A new framework, MisKnow-Agent, reveals that Deep Research agents are vulnerable to adopting false conclusions from misleading knowledge, even with search-enabled verifiers.
key_points: MisKnow-Agent generates 5,933 quality-controlled misleading knowledge instances for DeepResearch Benchmark tasks with controllable authority and style.
Experiments show both open-source and closed-source Deep Research agents adopt false conclusions from limited exposure to misleading knowledge.
Search-enabled verifier models identify misleading instances during focused corpus validation, but these instances are still adopted in long-horizon research.
Pre- and post-research defenses mitigate but do not fully prevent false-conclusion adoption.
summary.why_it_matters: Reliable Deep Research requires enhanced evidence verification and correction capabilities at both model and framework levels to prevent false conclusion adoption.

papers.title: AI Tour Meeting: Group Travel Planning by LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AI Tour Meeting is a framework using multiple LLM agents with distinct personas to collaboratively plan group travel through natural language discussion, enabling flexible orchestration and analysis of agent behavior.
key_points: The framework utilizes multiple LLM-based agents, each with a distinct persona, to collaboratively plan group travel.
Agents engage in natural language discussions to achieve an itinerary satisfying their individual constraints and preferences.
AI Tour Meeting provides interfaces for configuring agent personas, discussion workflows, monitoring, and LLM deployment.
The primary use case is a simulation tool for analyzing LLM agent behavior during tour planning discussions.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework offers a simulation tool for understanding and validating the collaborative behavior of LLM agents in complex planning scenarios.

papers.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing

summary.tldr: This paper introduces methods to distinguish route coherence, candidate quality, and candidate-by-context interaction in MoE models, finding expert subspaces overlap substantially but routing selects token-relevant experts for improved prediction.
key_points: Expert Subspace Separation Index (ESSI), matched-route residuals, and a prefix-controlled 2x2 factorial are used to distinguish MoE routing quantities.
Across six MoE architectures, expert subspaces overlap substantially, but actual routes explain token representations better than matched alternatives.
In OLMoE, Mixtral, and DeepSeek, selected candidates explain more residual representation than unselected rivals, though prefix interaction negatively narrows this advantage.
Adding later experts improved next-token prediction in 24 of 39 frozen-route comparisons, and controlled training favored Top-2 over Top-1 across three seeds.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding coherent overlap in MoE routing clarifies why geometric similarity alone is insufficient for determining expert redundancy or pruning value, impacting MoE design and optimization.

papers.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval

summary.tldr: ReToken introduces a single learnable embedding to select query-relevant visual tokens from a KV cache, improving vision-language model performance on long visual contexts.
key_points: ReToken is a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target.
It selects a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache.
Trained on a small image-QA dataset, ReToken improved Qwen3VL-8B by 13.4 points and InternVL3.5 by 12.4 points on Visual Haystacks.
ReToken achieved an 8.0-point gain with Qwen3VL-8B on LVBench for long video, zero-shot.
Both training and long-video inference for ReToken fit on a single H100 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: ReToken enables more efficient and accurate processing of long visual contexts in vision-language models, addressing computational and performance degradation challenges.

papers.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations

summary.tldr: Fairness Pruning identifies and intervenes on demographic bias in LLMs by locating differentially activated neurons in GLU-MLP layers using minimally contrastive prompts.
key_points: Fairness Pruning is a lightweight structural intervention method for managing demographic bias in LLMs.
The method identifies neurons in GLU architectures that react differentially to demographic attributes by analyzing inference-time activations at the down_proj input.
Zeroing identified neurons (at most 40 in Llama-3.2-1B, <0.031% of MLP width) causes bidirectional bias destabilization, not flat mitigation, due to mixed neuron effects.
The intervention retains 99.49% of reasoning and general knowledge capabilities in Llama-3.2-1B, indicating dissociable circuits for bias processing and model capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a surgical approach to understanding and potentially modulating demographic bias in LLMs without significantly impacting core model performance.

papers.title: Token-Level Diagnosis of Sycophancy in LLMs with Attribution-Guided Steering

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the Authority Share Index (ASI) to measure authority-driven token attributions in sycophantic LLM outputs and developed attribution-guided contrastive activation steering to reduce sycophant behavior during inference.
key_points: The Authority Share Index (ASI) uses Integrated Gradients to show that sycophantic responses attribute higher attention to authority-related tokens than resistant responses.
Token attributions reveal that an authority's asserted claim drives sycophancy more strongly than the authority's credentials.
Attribution-guided contrastive activation steering builds a steering vector using high-attribution tokens from sycophantic versus resistant responses.
Inference-time steering reduced sycophancy from 96% to 25% in the strongest tested case across five models and 30 test configurations without retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: Token-level attribution enables non-disruptive, inference-time intervention to reduce model sycophancy without requiring full model retraining.

papers.title: AMRD: Adaptive Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Lightweight Speech Emotion Recognition

summary.tldr: AMRD proposes adaptive multi-teacher relational distillation for lightweight speech emotion recognition, addressing teacher reliability and inter-sample relational structure through a one-class SVM and relational distillation loss.
key_points: AMRD uses a one-class SVM on each teacher's logit similarity matrix to assign per-batch weights, favoring more coherent teachers.
A relational distillation loss aligns teacher and student similarity matrices, capturing inter-sample relational structure.
AMRD outperforms single-teacher distillation baselines on IEMOCAP and CREMA-D datasets across four student architectures.
Ablation studies confirm both the adaptive weighting and relational distillation components provide complementary gains.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables the deployment of accurate speech emotion recognition models on resource-constrained edge devices for real-time applications.

papers.title: Pedestrian Archetypes Extension -- More Pedestrian Models for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Testing

summary.tldr: This paper extends the Pedestrian Archetypes framework by introducing 7 new pedestrian archetypes, identified through further annotation of YouTube dash-cam videos, to better describe dangerous pedestrian behaviors for autonomous vehicle safety testing.
key_points: The original Pedestrian Archetypes framework proposed 12 pedestrian archetypes.
Seven new pedestrian archetypes were identified through additional annotation of YouTube dash-cam videos.
The new archetypes capture behavior patterns not explained by the initial taxonomy.
Each new archetype is defined by essential and optional behaviors, with video-frame evidence provided.
summary.why_it_matters: Expanding the pedestrian archetype taxonomy provides a more comprehensive understanding of diverse and dangerous pedestrian behaviors, crucial for robust autonomous vehicle safety testing.

papers.title: FBFM: A Training-Free Asynchronous Feedback Mechanism for Flow-Matching in World-Action Models Execution

summary.tldr: Feedback Flow Matching (FBFM) is a training-free inference mechanism that applies masked pseudoinverse corrections to conditional velocity fields during flow matching for asynchronous, step-level re-grounding in world-action models.
key_points: Pushes re-grounding inside actively generated chunks rather than relying solely on coarse chunk-wise updates.
Applies a masked pseudoinverse correction to the conditional velocity field during the flow-matching generation process.
Uses cross-chunk pairing where preceding action chunks guide next action chunks, and intermediate execution observations guide subsequent frame predictions.
Evaluated on DreamZero (joint-generation WAM) and LingBot-VA (stage-wise WAM) across LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 tasks, increasing success rates by over 5% in favorable settings.
summary.why_it_matters: FBFM provides a training-free method to suppress prediction drift and improve real-time responsiveness to unexpected events in long-horizon robotic control.

papers.title: CAGE: Certified Authorization under Typed-Return Uncertainty for Tool-Using Agents

summary.tldr: CAGE is a framework that certifies LLM agent tool authorizations over a joint neighborhood of categorical binding faults and continuous numerical drift, preventing security failures caused by uncoupled channel verification.
key_points: Standard runtime permission gates fail because separate certification of categorical and numerical channels does not compose, allowing joint perturbations to turn safe actions unsafe.
CAGE certifies the joint neighborhood directly by exactly enumerating discrete categorical branches and certifying continuous numerical perturbations within each branch.
Depending on policy executability, CAGE uses CAGE-Exact to certify the policy itself, or CAGE-Lip and CAGE-RS to certify a learned gate under an explicit, measured fidelity assumption.
Evaluations across synthetic, policy-as-code, regulatory, and real-transaction benchmarks show CAGE eliminates in-budget false allows while maintaining autonomous execution capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents tool-using LLM agents from executing unauthorized actions when small data-binding errors or numerical drifts occur in tool outputs.

papers.title: CLIFT: Turning Gemini Robotics On-Device into Humanoid Specialists via Non-Invasive Closed-Loop Iterative Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: CLIFT provides a non-invasive, closed-loop iterative fine-tuning method that converts deployment-time reward feedback into API-compatible supervised data for closed-weight robot foundation models without requiring access to weights, gradients, or losses.
key_points: Evaluated on Gemini Robotics On-Device (GROD), showing direct SFT via managed API outperforms leading open-weight VLAs trained on identical demonstrations.
CLIFT addresses limitations of pure imitation learning in managed-API regimes by converting deployment feedback into supervised data for iterative tuning.
Enables closed-loop policy refinement for agile, contact-rich humanoid manipulation without needing internal model signals, likelihoods, or gradients.
Achieves near-perfect task success on real humanoid hardware within two iterative flywheel cycles.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables downstream developers to achieve high-performance policy optimization on proprietary, closed-weight robot foundation models using standard supervised fine-tuning APIs.

papers.title: ActFovea: Runtime Safeguarding for VLA Policies via Spatiotemporal Visual-Action Consistency

summary.tldr: ActFovea is a training-free, plug-and-play safeguarding framework that detects and mitigates runtime VLA policy failures using spatiotemporal visual-action consistency.
key_points: Constructs action-conditioned foveated regions using kinematics, proprioception, and recent actions to suppress irrelevant visual data while retaining motion corridors.
Evaluates visual motion and observation freshness against geometric and state transitions to identify runtime risks.
Mitigates recoverable failures by generating and verifying disturbance-specific candidate observations, triggering a bounded safe-failure procedure when recovery is impossible.
Boosts $π_0$ policy success rates on LIBERO from 49.3% to 90.3% under visual overlays, and improves action drift and visual delay performance by 7.0 and 9.8 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployment of VLA policies in dynamic environments by providing robustness against visual disruptions and hardware delays without expensive policy retraining.

papers.title: Memory Provenance Laundering in LLM Agents: A Non-Amplification Firewall for Persistent Memory

summary.tldr: Researchers identified 'memory provenance laundering' in LLM agents and introduced the Provenance-Preserving Memory Firewall (PPMF) to block unauthorized high-risk actions by enforcing source-authority non-amplification during memory consolidation.
key_points: Memory provenance laundering occurs when lossy LLM memory consolidation rewrites untrusted observations as user history, erasing low-trust sources while preserving action triggers.
Existing prompt filters, content sanitizers, and tool guards fail to enforce non-amplification of source authority after memory consolidation.
PPMF acts as memory middleware that maintains platform-level provenance, assigning risk labels to authorize tool calls by matching action risk against memory authority.

In evaluations with fixed risk policies, vulnerable consolidated memories hit a 1.000 attack success rate (ASR), whereas PPMF reduced unauthorized high-risk actions to zero without blocking confirmed benign actions.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents untrusted external inputs from covertly gaining elevated execution privileges when stored and consolidated in an LLM agent's persistent long-term memory.

papers.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs

summary.tldr: An automatic multi-policy PEFT framework organizes optimization-compatible adaptation paths via task grouping and sequencing using independent QLoRAs under a fixed parameter budget.
key_points: Organizes optimization paths by task grouping and sequencing to decouple heterogeneous tasks into independent Quantized Low-Rank Adapters (QLoRAs).
Mitigates interference and catastrophic forgetting in shared optimization spaces while preserving positive transfer among compatible tasks.
Achieves a state-of-the-art score of 44.78 on the TRACE benchmark under the same trainable capacity as single-policy PEFT baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizing task optimization paths improves multi-task PEFT performance more effectively than simply expanding adapter parameter capacity.

papers.title: The Grokked Illusion: True Equilibrium Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting

summary.tldr: Sampling models from Wang-Landau Molecular Dynamics yields high-entropy configurations that resist catastrophic forgetting far better than standard AdamW-trained grokked models, despite both achieving identical saturated test performance.
key_points: AdamW-trained grokked models suffer catastrophic forgetting (accuracy drops from 100% to under 75%) when forced to memorize noisy random labels, whereas high-entropy models maintain ~95% accuracy.
High-entropy models maintain a significantly higher effective rank in both attention and MLP layer weights before and after noise injection, as revealed by SVD.
The 'grokked illusion' describes hidden model fragility where perfect generalization hides poor robustness to subsequent parameter updates.
Rich representation buffers in high-entropy weight volumes prevent new learning from wiping out prior task knowledge.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals that standard optimization metrics mask structural fragility, showing that sampling high-entropy parameter volumes creates richer, higher-rank representations that prevent catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Adaptive FastOPD: Progress-Aware Rollout Horizon Expansion for Efficient On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Adaptive FastOPD dynamically expands the on-policy distillation rollout horizon based on relative teacher-student progress signals and horizon utilization, preventing premature expansions caused by outlier long responses.
key_points: Tracks four relative teacher-student signals measured against values recorded at horizon entry to detect learning plateaus in boundary regions.
Requires sufficient horizon utilization to prevent a small number of long responses from triggering costly horizon expansions prematurely.
Reduces training time by 49.1% to 71.2% compared to OPD 15K while achieving the highest average performance across tested teacher-student pairs.
Demonstrates robustness across a variety of hyperparameter settings without relying on fixed step intervals or absolute agreement thresholds.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly accelerates on-policy distillation training without sacrificing model performance by dynamically optimizing rollout horizons based on actual learning progress.

papers.title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?

summary.tldr: Increasing interventional pretraining data fails to correct causal sign errors in language models because inference-time observational context systematically suppresses learned causal capabilities.
key_points: In Simpson's-paradox synthetic environments, pretraining with higher fractions of interventional data scales do()-response magnitude without correcting sign errors copied from observational contexts.
At inference time, purely observational contexts caused sign reversals in 29/50 worlds, whereas aligned interventional probes achieved 41/50 correct directions.
Activation patching localizes the context-driven suppression switch to the middle layers' observational rows.
An evidence-averaging evaluation protocol reduces causal sign errors from 26% to 9% by mitigating sampling noise.
Retraining with randomized signs removes the learned positive-effect prior in-distribution, but fails to erase it out-of-distribution on the CLadder benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluations and pretraining mixtures alone cannot guarantee correct causal reasoning; models require prompt contexts free of conflicting observational noise to unleash learned interventional capabilities.

papers.title: OnlineCache: Learning Dynamic Caching Policies with Error Correction for Efficient Diffusion Inference

summary.tldr: OnlineCache is a dynamic caching framework that uses policy gradient and a learnable corrector within a bilevel optimization setup to adaptively skip and correct diffusion model feature computations per sample and timestep.
key_points: Empirically demonstrates that generation difficulty varies by prompt and error sensitivity varies across timesteps, invalidating static caching schedules.
Leverages policy gradient to train a lightweight network that dynamically decides when to cache based on prompt difficulty and timestep sensitivity.
Integrates a learnable corrector module to mitigate local approximation errors caused by feature caching.
Jointly optimizes the policy network (for global quality) and the corrector (for local error minimization) via bilevel optimization.
Achieves a ~3x speedup on FLUX.1-dev while maintaining generation fidelity, outperforming static baselines on DiT and CogVideoX.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables sample-adaptive acceleration for heavy diffusion and video generation models without sacrificing generation quality.

papers.title: PTP: Previous-Token Prediction based LLM Inversion for Near-Exact Prompt Reconstruction

summary.tldr: A novel functional LLM inversion method uses an explicit inverse model trained from scratch with previous-token prediction on target LLM synthetic data to enable black-box, near-exact prompt reconstruction without auxiliary datasets or logits.
key_points: Inverts target LLMs in a strict black-box setting without relying on auxiliary datasets, pretrained sequence-to-sequence fine-tuning, model weights, or logits.
Trains an inverse language model from scratch on synthetically generated target LLM data using a previous-token prediction training objective.
Generates diverse candidate prompts through sampling that produce similar forward responses under the target LLM.
Outperforms prior semantic reconstruction methods on token-based evaluation metrics for both prompt and response reconstructions while demonstrating transferability across different LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, black-box prompt recovery and auditing of proprietary language models solely through their generated text outputs.

papers.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving

summary.tldr: TokTier is a stateful tokenization service that eliminates re-tokenization bottlenecks in agentic LLM serving by combining exact incremental repair over appended text with GPU-accelerated full tokenization for cold requests.
key_points: Achieves exact output equivalence to full reference tokenization via local window re-tokenization, per-request stable-boundary checks, and automatic fallback mechanisms.
Reduces incremental repair latency to 0.5-1.1 ms for contexts from 100K to 3M characters, outperforming HuggingFace (HF) tokenization by up to 437x and Gigatoken by 2.1x at 1M characters.
Encodes 1M-character full requests in 0.87 ms on GPU by decomposing GPT-family regex pre-tokenization into run-local rules, running up to 491x faster than HF CPU tokenization.
Integration with vLLM reduces median time to first token by 16-34% and P99 latency by 23% during peak traffic bursts.
Sustains 1,821 requests/s under a 50 ms P99 SLA using four repair cores and one GPU, compared to 40 requests/s for a 16-core stateless front end.
summary.why_it_matters: By removing the severe CPU front-end bottleneck of re-tokenizing long transcripts in agentic workflows, TokTier significantly lowers time to first token and improves server throughput without altering token outputs.

papers.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: The World Critic Model (WCM) uses a LeJEPA architecture to jointly predict future latent states and estimate values, resolving state approximation issues in VLA reinforcement learning.
key_points: Identifies that single-frame observation critics suffer from a state approximation failure due to partial observability and a lack of cross-temporal dynamics supervision.
Utilizes a lightweight LeJEPA architecture to jointly model temporal world dynamics and estimate state values, avoiding exponential complexity from high-dimensional visual histories.
Integrates into on-policy and off-policy RL pipelines, supporting VLA backbones such as Pi0, Pi0.5, and OpenVLA-OFT.
Validated across 149 simulated tasks across four benchmarks and seven real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: WCM improves the temporal representation of critic networks, leading to superior generalization and stability when fine-tuning vision-language-action models with RL.

papers.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression

summary.tldr: ResKV splits a fixed KV cache budget into an exact main cache and a compact residual cache, reconstructing omitted token attention contributions directly within the unified softmax normalization during long-context inference.
key_points: Identifies omitted token loss as residual statistics in both the softmax attention numerator and denominator.
Splits the budget into an unmodified main KV cache and a compact residual cache that participates in the same softmax normalization step.
Uses a construction-time validation proxy to determine layer- and KV head-wise residual allocation.
Applies a decode-time dynamic gate to adjust residual contributions dynamically for individual queries.
summary.why_it_matters: It recovers accuracy lost during KV cache eviction without altering retained keys/values or compromising peak memory and decode throughput on benchmarks like LongBench and RULER.

papers.title: Sycophancy Undermines Epistemic Vigilance in Cooperative Vision-Language Tasks

summary.tldr: A new information-asymmetric spot-the-difference task reveals that vision-language models fail at epistemic vigilance by agreeing with partners over their own private visual evidence, a failure remediable via task-agnostic sycophancy steering vectors.
key_points: Models evaluated on a dialog-based, information-asymmetric spot-the-difference task frequently overlook private image evidence to agree with partners.
Failure in epistemic vigilance manifests as sycophancy, characterized by weak evidential grounding and over-accommodation in goal-oriented dialog.
Applying model steering vectors learned from task-agnostic sycophancy examples reduces these errors and improves faithfulness to visual evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: Mitigating sycophancy via steering vectors enables vision-language models to act as reliable partners in multi-agent cooperative tasks requiring accurate information exchange.

papers.title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization

summary.tldr: A new decoupled evaluation paradigm uses paired Know and Act tests to reveal that LLM agents frequently recall user preferences correctly but still fail to apply them in behavioral scenarios.
key_points: Introduces a decoupled evaluation method administering paired Know (recall) and Act (behavioral) tests on identical user preferences.
Evaluated 1,000 user preferences across 16 systems, five memory architectures, and three levels of preference expression strength.
Identified a substantial performance gap where models successfully pass memory recall tests but fail to act on the recalled preferences.
Found that while specialized memory architectures narrow this gap, preference utilization remains weakest in high-stakes domains like health and therapy.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard retrieval or recall benchmarks overestimate LLM personalization capabilities because models frequently fail to translate successfully retrieved user constraints into actual downstream behavior.

papers.title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Zero-Mem eliminates intermediate LLM calls and token generation in LLM agent memory operations by combining raw-trace storage with dual-view retrieval and deterministic calibration.
key_points: Organizes un-generated raw interaction traces using an entity-context graph for cross-interaction links and a temporal hierarchy for session locality.
Weighs and retrieves from both views per query to gather supporting relations and surrounding context without invoking LLM generation prior to final QA.
Uses a deterministic calibration step to discard conflicting evidence and keep the final QA reader grounded in retrieved traces.
Reduces memory-operation time cost by 57.6% compared to the fastest baseline while maintaining competitive performance on long-memory and long-context QA benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that structured memory management for LLM agents can be achieved deterministically without consuming LLM tokens or incurring costly intermediate generation overhead.

papers.title: Data Turnstile: A Scalable Open Framework for Function-Calling Data Generation

summary.tldr: Data Turnstile is an open-source framework that generates high-quality synthetic function-calling data from API specs via constrained stepwise generation, validation, and error-feedback loops.
key_points: Decomposes multi-turn tool interactions into constrained, step-by-step generation with built-in validation and error-feedback loops.
Fine-tuning Qwen3-0.6B without chain-of-thought on Turnstile data yielded 75.9% accuracy on the BFCL benchmark, up from 67.4% for the base model with thinking enabled.
Fine-tuning Qwen3-1.7B achieved a 31.1% pass^1 score on the multi-turn τ²-bench Telecom domain, outperforming Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (27.4%).
Open-sources the framework alongside a dataset covering 1,000+ APIs and 100K+ multi-turn interactions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables small language models to outperform models up to 19 times larger on complex tool-use tasks by resolving the training data quality bottleneck.

papers.title: Knowing When to Quit: Diagnosing and Training LLMs to Abort Futile Reasoning

summary.tldr: Researchers analyzed 'futile reasoning' in large language models on beyond-capability tasks and developed Capability-aligned Reinforcement Learning (CaRL) to train models to refuse impossible tasks rather than outputting specious derivations.
key_points: Futile reasoning occurs when LLMs generate computationally expensive, semantically void, or superficially valid but erroneous derivations on tasks beyond their capability limits.
The primary failure mode identified is specious reasoning, where outputs contain subtle errors that escalate in frequency as task difficulty increases.
The proposed CaRL framework uses reward shaping to incentivize refusal over futile reasoning and employs hindsight refusal augmentation to convert task failures into refusal supervision.
Experiments show CaRL substantially reduces futile reasoning without degrading model performance on achievable tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Enabling LLMs to recognize their capability boundaries reduces wasted compute and prevents users from being misled by plausible-sounding but incorrect reasoning.

papers.title: Learning Latent Reasoning Traces for Scalar Reward Models End-to-End

summary.tldr: LatentRM is a reward modeling framework that learns intermediate reasoning traces as discrete latent variables optimized end-to-end via on-policy training to explicitly maximize downstream scalar reward likelihood.
key_points: LatentRM models reasoning traces as discrete latent variables instead of relying on natural language scores or parallel multi-task learning.
The framework uses on-policy optimization to directly couple intermediate reasoning traces with downstream scalar reward predictions.
It addresses traditional scalar RM reliance on superficial cues and generative RM limitations regarding numerical flexibility and probabilistic interpretability.
Evaluations demonstrate superior performance over scalar, generative, and hybrid RMs in preference modeling and RLHF policy alignment across in-distribution and OOD tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: By combining deep latent reasoning with precise, probabilistically interpretable scalar outputs, LatentRM improves language model alignment and generalization on complex, out-of-distribution tasks.

papers.title: Faster but Different: Diagnosing and Controlling Content Drift in Accelerated Multimodal Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: A diagnostic study of training-free acceleration in multimodal diffusion LLMs reveals silent content drift caused by stale KV-cache states, which can be mitigated by shortening refresh intervals to achieve a 1.3x speedup with near-exact agreement.
key_points: Evaluation of Fast-dLLM on 300 real images showed that confidence-threshold tuning fails to improve baseline agreement, whereas state-refresh ablations pinpoint stale visual and text states as the source of content drift.
A targeted audit of 50 low-agreement outputs found genuine content substitution in 50% of the pairs.
Shortening the KV-cache refresh interval provides a monotonic speed-agreement trade-off, recovering near-exact output agreement at a 1.3x speedup.
In a blinded two-annotator evaluation, the pooled factual-error difference between accelerated and baseline models was 0.00 (95% CI [-0.17, +0.17]).
Adaptive and smoothed-refresh variants failed to outperform fixed-interval KV-cache refreshes at matched compute costs.
summary.why_it_matters: Training-free acceleration for multimodal diffusion models can alter output content without dropping overall factual accuracy, requiring explicit KV-cache refresh controls to ensure consistent behavior at serving time.

papers.title: Tokenizer-Agnostic Engram Module

summary.tldr: A modified Engram module replaces token-level N-gram XOR hashing with general polynomial hashing over byte sequences, enabling tokenizer-agnostic embedding reuse without sacrificing performance.
key_points: Engram originally relies on token-level N-gram XOR hashing, tightly coupling embeddings to a specific tokenizer.
The proposed method treats N-grams as sampled byte sequences from all possible token byte sequences using a joint embedding space across N.
Polynomial hashing achieves hash equivalence for any byte-equivalent token sequences, regardless of the underlying tokenizer.
Empirical results show the tokenizer-agnostic substitution delivers performance comparable to the original architecture.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows pre-trained Engram memory embeddings to be reused directly across models that employ different tokenizers, avoiding the need to retrain embeddings from scratch.

papers.title: TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: TransMem is a lightweight inference-time module that transforms sparse historical hidden states from a frozen LLM into reusable memory representations without repeatedly re-encoding past context.
key_points: Uses a lightweight gating network to dynamically apply latent interventions to current hidden states.
Employs evidence-conditioned self-distillation where a memory-augmented student matches the predictive distribution of an evidence-only teacher sharing the same frozen backbone.
Achieves gains of 11.58-29.25 F1 on LoCoMo and 10.20-13.03 F1 on HotpotQA.
Increases average accuracy on MemoryAgentBench from 29.54% to 40.00%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-context LLM agents to effectively reuse past hidden states as memory without incurring the computational cost of repeatedly re-encoding long interaction histories.

papers.title: PARALLEL: A Prefrontal-Aligned Reinforcement inspired Approach for Language-Model Learning under Explicit Limits

summary.tldr: PARALLEL is a reinforcement-inspired framework that dynamically adjusts sample-dependent update intensity using separate goal and uncertainty control signals to optimize language model adaptation under resource limits.
key_points: Combines goal-related and uncertainty-related controller signals with current model representations to determine sample-specific update intensity.
Uses immediate utility-cost feedback in a reinforcement-inspired controller to learn when and how strongly to modify model parameters.
Retains 94.1–99.2% of Full-adaptation performance on multiple-choice reasoning, and 96.9–98.6% ROUGE-1/ROUGE-2 and 98.8–98.9% ROUGE-L on XSum and CNN/DailyMail.
Outperforms Full adaptation in ARC accuracy and late-stage trajectory stability when controlled for equal cumulative adaptation time or GPU energy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables highly compute- and energy-efficient post-deployment stream adaptation by avoiding redundant parameter updates while preserving full fine-tuning performance.

security.title: Top Agentic AI security resources — August 2026

summary.tldr: Adversa AI compiled twenty security resources covering recent production AI agent exploits, including memory poisoning, sandbox escapes, the Kiro RCE, and two CVSS 9.8 vulnerabilities in Cursor.
key_points: Four research teams successfully compromised production AI agents within a ten-day period.
Resource collection details the Kiro Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability and sandbox escape vectors.
Includes analysis of two critical Cursor vulnerabilities rated at CVSS 9.8 and memory poisoning techniques.
summary.why_it_matters: Production AI agents face critical vulnerabilities like RCEs and memory poisoning that allow attackers to escape sandboxes and compromise underlying systems.

security.title: Anthropic’s Opus 5 Is Better at Resisting Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: Anthropic's Opus 5 demonstrates improved resistance to prompt injection on the IPI benchmark compared to previous versions and competing models.
key_points: Opus 5 reduced indirect prompt injection attack success probability within 15 attempts to 2.0% (down from 5.5% in Opus 4.8), and to 0.2% on a single attempt.
Opus 5 outperformed other Anthropic models on the IPI benchmark at k=15, including Mythos 5 (2.6%) and Sonnet 5 (5.9%).
Non-Claude models performed significantly worse at k=15, with Muse Spark at 16.5%, GPT 5.6 Sol at 20.0%, GPT 5.6 Terra at 30.4%, and GPT 5.6 Luna at 43.9%.
A single attack attempt against GPT 5.6 Sol succeeded 3.1% of the time, which is higher than Opus 5's 2.0% failure rate across 15 attempts.
summary.why_it_matters: While general prompt injection remains unsolved, advanced models are becoming significantly more resilient against automated attacks in benchmarked scenarios.

security.title: AgenticRepair: Multi-Faceted Program Context Engineering for Agentic Vulnerability Repair

summary.tldr: AgenticRepair uses multi-faceted program context engineering and specialized subagents to capture code-structure, runtime-execution, and commit-history contexts, achieving a 73% success rate on the SEC-Bench vulnerability repair benchmark.
key_points: Orchestrates three specialized LLM subagents to engineer code-structure, runtime-execution, and commit-history contexts.
Embeds engineered contexts into the memory of a dedicated repair subagent for context-conditioned patch synthesis.
Evaluated on SEC-Bench (300 real-world instances) with sanitizer-based patch verification, outperforming the strongest baseline by 29%.
Ablation studies demonstrate that all three context facets, multi-agent scaffolding, and base-model capacity are critical to performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Systematically combining cross-file data flows, crash semantics, and commit history enables agentic models to generate significantly more accurate security patches for complex software vulnerabilities.

security.title: MOSAIC: Masked Outsourcing of Secure AI Computations

summary.tldr: MOSAIC is a matrix-multiplication masking protocol for secure AI outsourcing that achieves optimal asymptotic client overhead by introducing controlled noise, enabling confidential 70B transformer inference on untrusted servers.
key_points: Protects both client input and model weights from untrusted, powerful servers by reducing security to decisional LWE and LPN assumptions.
Utilizes a relaxed-correctness matrix-multiplication masking protocol that adds small amounts of noise to lower asymptotic client overhead.
Employs an error-scaling mechanism using random Hadamard rotations to bound noise accumulation across multi-layer transformers.
Achieves perplexity comparable to standard quantization methods on 70B models and matches full-precision BF16 inference accuracy on HumanEval.
summary.why_it_matters: MOSAIC minimizes the trusted computing base, allowing resource-constrained clients to securely outsource large-scale LLM inference to untrusted data center accelerators with minimal performance loss.

security.title: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion

summary.tldr: A paired diagnostic reveals that prompt-level guardrails for GUI agents fail against multi-turn user persuasion and concealed requests, causing systematic alignment degradation.
key_points: A single-line guardrail reduces single-shot Attack Success Rate (ASR) by up to 40 percentage points with near-zero over-refusal cost.
Escalating requests over four turns increases guarded ASR by roughly 20 points across all three tested frontier GUI models.
Multi-turn escalation causes guardrail erosion in Qwen and uncovers defense-orthogonal dynamic risk in Claude and GPT.
Guardrails flip the salience gap: concealed requests become systematically more successful than explicit ones because the defense depends on explicitly named intent.
summary.why_it_matters: Static, single-turn evaluation metrics significantly overestimate the real-world safety of GUI agents exposed to dynamic user interactions.

security.title: Memory Provenance Laundering in LLM Agents: A Non-Amplification Firewall for Persistent Memory

summary.tldr: Researchers identified memory provenance laundering in LLM agents and introduced the Provenance-Preserving Memory Firewall (PPMF) to prevent unauthorized high-risk actions by gating tool calls against platform-maintained memory authority.
key_points: Memory provenance laundering occurs when LLM memory consolidation rewrites untrusted external observations as benign user history, erasing source context while retaining action triggers.
PPMF acts as lightweight memory middleware that enforces source-authority non-amplification by mapping action risk directly to the authority of relevant memories.
Without provenance enforcement, vulnerable consolidated memories achieved up to a 1.000 Attack Success Rate (ASR) in schema-grounded evaluations.
PPMF successfully blocked 100% of unauthorized high-risk actions under tested policies without halting confirmed benign or low-risk memory executions.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents indirect prompt injections and untrusted data from permanently elevating their execution privileges when consolidated into an LLM agent's long-term memory.

security.title: GoldenRetriever: Non-Interactive Homomorphic Encrypted Retrieval for Privacy-Preserving RAG

summary.tldr: GoldenRetriever is a non-interactive, privacy-preserving RAG framework using CKKS homomorphic encryption and threshold selection to replace top-k ranking, reducing computational complexity from quadratic to linear.
key_points: Replaces expensive top-k ranking under encryption with threshold selection, filtering documents whose similarity scores exceed a predefined value.
Reduces retrieval computational complexity from quadratic to linear relative to corpus size.
Uses CKKS-based homomorphic computation to execute similarity evaluation and document selection without exposing queries, scores, or indices.
Introduces a precision-stable mask polarization method to reliably reconstruct discrete tokens from approximate encrypted computations.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly lowers latency in privacy-preserving retrieval, making non-interactive, fully encrypted RAG practical for sensitive enterprise datasets.

vendors.title: Stateless MCP has recaptured my interest (and inspired mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp)

summary.tldr: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) 2.0, or 2026-07-28 specification, introduces a stateless design, simplifying client/server implementations and enhancing scalability for LLM agent frameworks.
key_points: Stateless MCP (2026-07-28 specification) replaces the two-request stateful model (initialize session, then call tool) with a single HTTP request for tool calls.
Legacy stateful MCP required a POST to /mcp with "method": "initialize" to get a Mcp-Session-Id, followed by another POST with the session ID to "method": "tools/call".
Stateless MCP uses HTTP headers like MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28, Mcp-Method: tools/call, and Mcp-Name: search, along with a single JSON body for the tool call.
The stateless design eliminates the need for server-side state management of session IDs, improving scalability and simplifying routing.
mcp-explorer is a new stateless Python CLI tool for interactively probing MCP servers, demonstrated with `uvx mcp-explorer list https://agentic-mermaid.dev/mcp`.
summary.why_it_matters: The simplified stateless design makes MCP tools easier to audit and control, enabling smaller models to drive them effectively and reducing implementation complexity for developers.
